memes.speaker: employee.a@sdworx.example
memes.statement: Contractor invoices received after the 25th are processed in the next month's payroll run.

quotes.speaker: employee.a@sdworx.example
quotes.text: So anything that comes in after the twentieth — no, sorry, the twenty-fifth — goes into next month's run.

quotes.speaker: employee.a@sdworx.example
quotes.text: So for the November run, if it arrives on the twenty-sixth, it's December.

quote.text: Yes, that's right, it was in the payroll newsletter in September.

memes.speaker: team.lead@sdworx.example
memes.statement: An urgent contractor invoice received after the cut-off can only be paid with the Team Lead's approval by e-mail before the payroll run is closed.

suggested.title: Urgent contractor invoices after the cut-off

quotes.speaker: team.lead@sdworx.example
quotes.text: So, an urgent invoice after the cut-off can still be paid, but only with my approval by e-mail before the run is closed.

quote.text: Yes, that's how we agreed it with Finance.

memes.speaker: employee.b@sdworx.example
memes.statement: Before the first payment to a new contractor, check their VAT number in VIES.

suggested.title: Check a new contractor's VAT number in VIES

quotes.speaker: employee.b@sdworx.example
quotes.text: Finance asked everyone to check a new contractor's VAT number in vies before the first payment.

quotes.speaker: employee.b@sdworx.example
quotes.text: It takes like one minute, you just enter the number on the European site.

traps.note: Small talk about the weekend and the coffee machine
Anecdote about last month's late invoices — case data
A's opinion about the rule, not a confirmation of its content

notes: Meme 1: the self-correction (twentieth → twenty-fifth) is inside the first quote; the statement uses the corrected value.
Meme 2: 'my approval' is resolved to 'the Team Lead's approval' (FR-MA2). Speaker and confirmer are both verifiers of the team (BR-M3).
Meme 3: 'vies' is a speech-recognition artifact, normalized to 'VIES' in the statement.
